jotai has exactly one subscription primitive, `store.sub(atom, cb)`, which fires when that atom's value changes. The scenario needs two kinds the library does not have: a read-projection registrant over a cold node that must never fire, and a commit-level registrant that fires on every commit regardless of which node changed. jotai has no commit boundary to subscribe to, so the property being measured — per-projection dispatch being O(1) rather than O(registrations) — has no expressible analogue. Simulating it with a hand-rolled "commit counter" atom would measure the simulation, not jotai.

jotai evaluates a derived chain by mutual recursion through readAtomState, with no iterative fallback. At a chain depth of 10000 the first mounted read exhausts V8's call stack (RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded) on the default 984 KiB main stack, so the graph cannot be constructed at all -- there is nothing to measure, at any number of repetitions. Shallower scales of the same scenario are measured normally.

mobx evaluates a computed chain by mutual recursion through its derivation graph, with no iterative fallback. At a chain depth of 10000 reading the tail exceeds the V8 call stack (RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded) on the default 984 KiB main stack, so the graph cannot be read at all -- there is nothing to measure, at any number of repetitions. Shallower scales of the same scenario are measured normally.

reselect evaluates a chained selector by recursive invocation, so reading the tail of a 10000-link chain recurses 10000 deep and exhausts the V8 call stack (RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded) on the default 984 KiB main stack -- during construction, before any timed region, so there is nothing to measure at any number of repetitions. Expressing this depth in redux would mean replacing reselect with a hand-rolled iterative evaluator, which would no longer be a reselect measurement. Shallower scales of the same scenario are measured normally.

ranking.exclusionReason: the runners are declared to do different amounts of work here and the difference is a constant multiple, not an overhead: `recomputeDivergence` puts the eager engines at 2L recomputes against the demand-driven engines' 0.4L at every scale, a flat 5x, over the 2x `comparabilityTolerance`. Separating push from pull is why the shape exists and the counts are the finding, but a wall-clock RANKING over a declared 5x is a restatement of the 5x. The cell is measured, published and still checked against `expectedRecomputes` -- it is held out of cross-library ranking only. `equivalenceOracle.readsPerStep` remains the quantity actually held equal across all five runners. Reconciling this means choosing one unit of work for the shape (see EQUIVALENCE.md, 'Repairing a non-comparable cell'), not writing down whichever count the runners happen to report.

jotai has exactly one subscription primitive, `store.sub(atom, cb)`, which fires when that atom's value changes. The scenario needs two kinds the library does not have: a read-projection registrant over a cold node that must never fire, and a commit-level registrant that fires on every commit regardless of which node changed. jotai has no commit boundary to subscribe to, so the property being measured — per-projection dispatch being O(1) rather than O(registrations) — has no expressible analogue. Simulating it with a hand-rolled "commit counter" atom would measure the simulation, not jotai.

jotai has no transaction and no atomic rollback. `store.set` commits per call, and a throw out of a write function or a derived getter leaves the already-written atoms written. The cell can only be imitated by catching the throw and re-issuing the prior value by hand, which measures a user-space workaround rather than an engine primitive, so it is reported as absent rather than as a comparable number.

reselect evaluates a chained selector by recursive invocation, so reading the tail of a 10000-link chain recurses 10000 deep and exhausts the V8 call stack (RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded) on the default 984 KiB main stack -- during construction, before any timed region, so there is nothing to measure at any number of repetitions. Expressing this depth in redux would mean replacing reselect with a hand-rolled iterative evaluator, which would no longer be a reselect measurement. Shallower scales of the same scenario are measured normally.

redux derivations are pull-based and evaluate after `dispatch` has already published the new state, so a throwing selector has no in-flight commit to unwind. The only redux-side number available would be a user-space compensating re-dispatch, which measures rollback *simulation* rather than the primitive this cell names. (The sibling cell `op-commit-rollback-1k` IS measured: a throw inside the reducer body aborts the Immer draft and leaves the store state untouched.)
measures the JS↔WASM `commit(state, action)` boundary of the causl backend. Redux Toolkit has no WebAssembly backend and no boundary to cross — there is no operation to compare against.
measures the bare wasm-bindgen scalar-call floor (`read_input(slot, gen) -> u64`) of the causl Rust bridge. Redux Toolkit is pure JavaScript; there is no bridge and no floor to measure.

isolates the BFS + Kahn topological walk inside causl's `recomputeAffected`. Redux has no propagation walk to isolate: dispatch runs one reducer and notifies every listener, and derivation order is whatever order readers happen to pull in. There is no corresponding data structure to probe.

jotai has exactly one subscription primitive, `store.sub(atom, cb)`, which fires when that atom's value changes. The scenario needs two kinds the library does not have: a read-projection registrant over a cold node that must never fire, and a commit-level registrant that fires on every commit regardless of which node changed. jotai has no commit boundary to subscribe to, so the property being measured — per-projection dispatch being O(1) rather than O(registrations) — has no expressible analogue. Simulating it with a hand-rolled "commit counter" atom would measure the simulation, not jotai.

jotai evaluates a derived chain by mutual recursion through readAtomState, with no iterative fallback. At a chain depth of 10000 the first mounted read exhausts V8's call stack (RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded) on the default 984 KiB main stack, so the graph cannot be constructed at all -- there is nothing to measure, at any number of repetitions. Shallower scales of the same scenario are measured normally.

mobx evaluates a computed chain by mutual recursion through its derivation graph, with no iterative fallback. At a chain depth of 10000 reading the tail exceeds the V8 call stack (RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded) on the default 984 KiB main stack, so the graph cannot be read at all -- there is nothing to measure, at any number of repetitions. Shallower scales of the same scenario are measured normally.

reselect evaluates a chained selector by recursive invocation, so reading the tail of a 10000-link chain recurses 10000 deep and exhausts the V8 call stack (RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded) on the default 984 KiB main stack -- during construction, before any timed region, so there is nothing to measure at any number of repetitions. Expressing this depth in redux would mean replacing reselect with a hand-rolled iterative evaluator, which would no longer be a reselect measurement. Shallower scales of the same scenario are measured normally.

ranking.exclusionReason: the runners are declared to do different amounts of work here and the difference is a constant multiple, not an overhead: `recomputeDivergence` puts the eager engines at 2L recomputes against the demand-driven engines' 0.4L at every scale, a flat 5x, over the 2x `comparabilityTolerance`. Separating push from pull is why the shape exists and the counts are the finding, but a wall-clock RANKING over a declared 5x is a restatement of the 5x. The cell is measured, published and still checked against `expectedRecomputes` -- it is held out of cross-library ranking only. `equivalenceOracle.readsPerStep` remains the quantity actually held equal across all five runners. Reconciling this means choosing one unit of work for the shape (see EQUIVALENCE.md, 'Repairing a non-comparable cell'), not writing down whichever count the runners happen to report.

Simulating it with a hand-rolled "commit counter" atom would measure the simulation, not jotai.

jotai evaluates a derived chain by mutual recursion through readAtomState, with no iterative fallback. At a chain depth of 10000 the first mounted read exhausts V8's call stack (RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded) on the default 984 KiB main stack, so the graph cannot be constructed at all -- there is nothing to measure, at any number of repetitions. Shallower scales of the same scenario are measured normally.

mobx evaluates a computed chain by mutual recursion through its derivation graph, with no iterative fallback. At a chain depth of 10000 reading the tail exceeds the V8 call stack (RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded) on the default 984 KiB main stack, so the graph cannot be read at all -- there is nothing to measure, at any number of repetitions. Shallower scales of the same scenario are measured normally.

reselect evaluates a chained selector by recursive invocation, so reading the tail of a 10000-link chain recurses 10000 deep and exhausts the V8 call stack (RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded) on the default 984 KiB main stack -- during construction, before any timed region, so there is nothing to measure at any number of repetitions. Expressing this depth in redux would mean replacing reselect with a hand-rolled iterative evaluator, which would no longer be a reselect measurement. Shallower scales of the same scenario are measured normally.

Separating push from pull is why the shape exists and the counts are the finding, but a wall-clock RANKING over a declared 5x is a restatement of the 5x. jotai has exactly one subscription primitive, `store.sub(atom, cb)`, which fires when that atom's value changes. The scenario needs two kinds the library does not have: a read-projection registrant over a cold node that must never fire, and a commit-level registrant that fires on every commit regardless of which node changed. jotai has no commit boundary to subscribe to, so the property being measured — per-projection dispatch being O(1) rather than O(registrations) — has no expressible analogue. Simulating it with a hand-rolled "commit counter" atom would measure the simulation, not jotai.

jotai has exactly one subscription primitive, `store.sub(atom, cb)`, which fires when that atom's value changes. The scenario needs two kinds the library does not have: a read-projection registrant over a cold node that must never fire, and a commit-level registrant that fires on every commit regardless of which node changed. jotai has no commit boundary to subscribe to, so the property being measured — per-projection dispatch being O(1) rather than O(registrations) — has no expressible analogue. Simulating it with a hand-rolled "commit counter" atom would measure the simulation, not jotai.

ranking.exclusionReason: the shapes are unrelated. causl's builder is `fanin(10000)` -- a plain fan-in with no cutoff and no fan-out, writing one input per step. mobx and jotai build scale/10 cutoff nodes over `scale` inputs plus an aggregate, and write EVERY input per step. Measured: causl-ts 1 recompute in 120.8 ms against mobx 1000 recomputes in 0.610 ms. This one reads against causl, which is the point: the rule is not here to flatter anybody. The two causl runners ALSO differ from each other here, which this reason did not say until #168: causl-ts builds width min(scale, 10000) and causl-wasm-ts builds width min(scale * 10, 10000), so causl-wasm-ts is saturated at 10000 from scale 1000 upward and its 1000->10000 segment is two readings of the same graph. Any comparison across this id has to be matched on WIDTH, not on scale.

jotai evaluates a derived chain by mutual recursion through readAtomState, with no iterative fallback. At a chain depth of 10000 the first mounted read exhausts V8's call stack (RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded) on the default 984 KiB main stack, so the graph cannot be constructed at all -- there is nothing to measure, at any number of repetitions. Shallower scales of the same scenario are measured normally.

mobx evaluates a computed chain by mutual recursion through its derivation graph, with no iterative fallback. At a chain depth of 10000 reading the tail exceeds the V8 call stack (RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded) on the default 984 KiB main stack, so the graph cannot be read at all -- there is nothing to measure, at any number of repetitions. Shallower scales of the same scenario are measured normally.

reselect evaluates a chained selector by recursive invocation, so reading the tail of a 10000-link chain recurses 10000 deep and exhausts the V8 call stack (RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded) on the default 984 KiB main stack -- during construction, before any timed region, so there is nothing to measure at any number of repetitions. Expressing this depth in redux would mean replacing reselect with a hand-rolled iterative evaluator, which would no longer be a reselect measurement. Shallower scales of the same scenario are measured normally.

jotai has no transaction and no atomic rollback. `store.set` commits per call, and a throw out of a write function or a derived getter leaves the already-written atoms written. The cell can only be imitated by catching the throw and re-issuing the prior value by hand, which measures a user-space workaround rather than an engine primitive, so it is reported as absent rather than as a comparable number.

ranking.exclusionReason: the runners agree they create 1000 derived nodes and disagree about what a creation costs, so the comparable quantity under this id is `creates` and not `recomputes`. The two eager runners now agree: causl-ts and causl-wasm-ts each evaluate the compute lambda ONCE per registration, off-bridge, with zero inbound __causl_compute crossings. WHAT CHANGED, because this entry declared otherwise until 2026-08-14: on clients 0.3.6 and 0.3.7 causl-wasm-ts evaluated it TWICE, once in the client graph layer, which is what discovers the ordered dependency set the engine RegisterDerived record needs, and once again in AuthoritativeWasmEngine.registerDerived, which primed the backend's own value cache. Client 0.5.0 carries causl-wasm-ts#279 slice S4, which hands registerDerived the value the graph layer already computed as a registration baseline (`{ value, at }`), so the priming evaluation is skipped whenever a baseline is supplied and only the discovery evaluation remains. Read out of the shipped 0.5.0 artefact rather than inferred: dist/wasm.js registerDerived reads `baseline === void 0 ? compute((depId) => this.read(depId)) : baseline.value`, and the graph layer's only call site passes `{ value: entry.value, at: entry.lastTime }`. The recompute and edgeReads divergences this entry used to declare for causl-wasm-ts are therefore gone, and the runner now matches the common declaration; the divergence on `unstable` and `dynamic-dep-flip` is NOT gone, because those reach the second evaluation through a post-commit rewire rather than through the registration, and the census still measures them at their declared counts. Measured through this runner's own census seam by `runners/causl-wasm-ts/probes/step-ops-census.mjs` on client 0.5.0: recomputes 1000, edgeReads 1000, creates 1001. The cell stays `non-comparable` regardless, and for a reason that has nothing to do with either eager runner: mobx computeds are lazy so its runner reads each one to match the eager engines and reports 1000; jotai and redux-rtk are lazy and read nothing, so both report 0. This cell was `unknown` until #166 established the mechanism.

jotai has no transaction and no atomic rollback. `store.set` commits per call, and a throw out of a write function or a derived getter leaves the already-written atoms written. The cell can only be imitated by catching the throw and re-issuing the prior value by hand, which measures a user-space workaround rather than an engine primitive, so it is reported as absent rather than as a comparable number.
mobx has no transactional rollback. A throw from inside a computed propagates to the reader and is cached, but no prior writes are unwound, so there is no rollback envelope to measure

redux derivations are pull-based and evaluate after `dispatch` has already published the new state, so a throwing selector has no in-flight commit to unwind. The only redux-side number available would be a user-space compensating re-dispatch, which measures rollback *simulation* rather than the primitive this cell names. (The sibling cell `op-commit-rollback-1k` IS measured: a throw inside the reducer body aborts the Immer draft and leaves the store state untouched.)

ranking.exclusionReason: the runners are declared to do different amounts of work here and the difference is a constant multiple, not an overhead: `recomputeDivergence` puts the eager engines at 2L recomputes against the demand-driven engines' 0.4L at every scale, a flat 5x, over the 2x `comparabilityTolerance`. Separating push from pull is why the shape exists and the counts are the finding, but a wall-clock RANKING over a declared 5x is a restatement of the 5x. The cell is measured, published and still checked against `expectedRecomputes` -- it is held out of cross-library ranking only. `equivalenceOracle.readsPerStep` remains the quantity actually held equal across all five runners. Reconciling this means choosing one unit of work for the shape (see EQUIVALENCE.md, 'Repairing a non-comparable cell'), not writing down whichever count the runners happen to report.

jotai evaluates a derived chain by mutual recursion through readAtomState, with no iterative fallback. At a chain depth of 10000 the first mounted read exhausts V8's call stack (RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded) on the default 984 KiB main stack, so the graph cannot be constructed at all -- there is nothing to measure, at any number of repetitions. Shallower scales of the same scenario are measured normally.

jotai has exactly one subscription primitive, `store.sub(atom, cb)`, which fires when that atom's value changes. The scenario needs two kinds the library does not have: a read-projection registrant over a cold node that must never fire, and a commit-level registrant that fires on every commit regardless of which node changed. jotai has no commit boundary to subscribe to, so the property being measured — per-projection dispatch being O(1) rather than O(registrations) — has no expressible analogue. Simulating it with a hand-rolled "commit counter" atom would measure the simulation, not jotai.

jotai has no transaction and no atomic rollback. `store.set` commits per call, and a throw out of a write function or a derived getter leaves the already-written atoms written. The cell can only be imitated by catching the throw and re-issuing the prior value by hand, which measures a user-space workaround rather than an engine primitive, so it is reported as absent rather than as a comparable number.

reselect evaluates a chained selector by recursive invocation, so reading the tail of a 10000-link chain recurses 10000 deep and exhausts the V8 call stack (RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded) on the default 984 KiB main stack -- during construction, before any timed region, so there is nothing to measure at any number of repetitions. Expressing this depth in redux would mean replacing reselect with a hand-rolled iterative evaluator, which would no longer be a reselect measurement. Shallower scales of the same scenario are measured normally.

redux derivations are pull-based and evaluate after `dispatch` has already published the new state, so a throwing selector has no in-flight commit to unwind. The only redux-side number available would be a user-space compensating re-dispatch, which measures rollback *simulation* rather than the primitive this cell names. (The sibling cell `op-commit-rollback-1k` IS measured: a throw inside the reducer body aborts the Immer draft and leaves the store state untouched.)
measures the JS↔WASM `commit(state, action)` boundary of the causl backend. Redux Toolkit has no WebAssembly backend and no boundary to cross — there is no operation to compare against.
measures the bare wasm-bindgen scalar-call floor (`read_input(slot, gen) -> u64`) of the causl Rust bridge. Redux Toolkit is pure JavaScript; there is no bridge and no floor to measure.

isolates the BFS + Kahn topological walk inside causl's `recomputeAffected`. Redux has no propagation walk to isolate: dispatch runs one reducer and notifies every listener, and derivation order is whatever order readers happen to pull in. There is no corresponding data structure to probe.
